_note: Approximate, verify. Mass, power, cost and stats are game-balance placeholders, not vendor figures. Each category has 2+ options so there are trade-offs. powerW is constant draw (negative) or sun-independent production (positive); solar arrays use stats.ratedPowerW. location "surface" parts do nothing in transit. Every recycler (waterRecoveryRate or oxygenRecoveryRate > 0) must draw power and have failureChancePerTurn.

items.name: Rigid Solar Array (5 kW)
items.description: Proven fold-out array. Cheap, but heavy for its output. Output scales with sunlight and drops as dust builds up.

items.name: Roll-Out Solar Array (10 kW)
items.description: Lightweight flexible blanket array. Twice the output for little extra mass, at almost three times the price.

items.name: Fission Surface Power (10 kW)
items.description: Small reactor that delivers steady power day and night, through dust storms. Very heavy and very expensive.

items.name: Lithium Battery Pack (50 kWh)
items.description: Standard battery modules. Cheap per kWh but heavy.

items.name: Lithium Battery Bank (150 kWh)
items.description: Three packs racked together. Enough for a short night, too heavy for a long one.

items.name: Regenerative Fuel Cell (200 kWh)
items.description: Splits water by day and recombines it at night. Much lighter per kWh than batteries, but expensive.

items.name: Low-Gain Antenna
items.description: Wide beam, no pointing needed. Very slow: fine for voice and telemetry, poor for science data.

items.name: High-Gain Antenna
items.description: Narrow-beam dish for high data rates. Must be pointed precisely at Earth.

items.name: Optical Laser Terminal
items.description: Laser link with enormous bandwidth. Expensive and blocked by clouds at the Earth station.

items.name: Ice Drill + Spectrometer
items.description: One-metre drill with an onboard spectrometer to confirm water ice in shadowed regolith.

items.name: Ground-Penetrating Radar
items.description: Maps buried ice layers. Light and cheap, but produces a lot of data to send home.

items.name: Sample Analysis Lab
items.description: Full lab for on-site analysis. Highest science return, but heavy and power-hungry.

items.name: Open-Loop Life Support
items.description: Simple air scrubbing with no water recycling. Light and cheap, but every litre of water must be launched.

items.name: Life Support Core (ECLSS)
items.description: Air revitalisation and 90% water recovery for a crew of four.

items.name: Advanced Water Recycler
items.description: Station-class recycler recovering 98% of water: the only way to make a two-year Mars stay fit on a rocket. Heavy, power-hungry, expensive, and it can break.

items.name: Water Recovery System (85%)
items.description: Mid-range distiller that recovers 85% of water from urine and humidity. Cheaper than the advanced recycler but packs more water.

items.name: Oxygen Generation Assembly
items.description: Splits water into oxygen and recovers oxygen from exhaled CO2, covering 75% of the crew's oxygen. Draws a lot of power.

items.name: Surface EVA Suit
items.description: Pressurised suit for surface work. One suit supports one crew member outside at a time.

items.name: EVA Suit Pair
items.description: Two suits so crew can always walk outside in pairs, the safe way.

items.name: Critical Spares Kit
items.description: Fuses, pumps, seals and connectors for the most likely failures.

items.name: Spares Crate
items.description: Three full repair kits. Heavy, but you can fix almost anything twice.

items.name: Unpressurised Mini Rover
items.description: Two-seat rover that reaches science sites beyond walking distance.

items.name: Pressurised Rover
items.description: Shirt-sleeve rover for multi-day traverses. Huge science reach, huge mass.

items.name: Lander Cabin (2 crew)
items.description: Cramped lander cabin. Light and cheap, but only fits two.

items.name: Inflatable Habitat (4 crew)
items.description: Packs small for launch and expands on the surface. Good volume for its mass.

items.name: Rigid Habitat (6 crew)
items.description: Station-style module with radiation shielding and room to spare. Very heavy.

items.name: Radiation Storm Shelter
items.description: Water-walled refuge where the crew hides during solar particle events. Blocks most of the dose; houses no one long-term.

items.name: Long-Stay Habitat (8 crew)
items.description: Two-deck surface base with storage for years of supplies. Enormous mass and power draw.
